text:
The evidence shows tree-cover loss in 2023, but it does not establish deforestation.

Hansen/UMD mapped about 0.7 ha of tree-cover loss in 2023 inside the asset, roughly 1.2% of its 58.1 ha. JRC data show the area was forest in 2020, and later years were observed, so the loss is corroborated under the method. A further 0.4 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

The MGAP 2021 map classes the affected area as planted forest (about 0.4 ha, Eucalyptus) or outside mapped forest (about 0.3 ha), with no native forest. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation, so this could be routine harvest. The data do not show whether land use changed.

The evidence also does not establish the cause, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance status. Answering the deforestation question would need additional evidence, such as post-loss land use or management records.
